main.summary: At Shravasti the Buddha tells Shariputra about the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and its teacher, Amitabha Buddha, and urges people to believe, to make the vow, and to hold the Buddha's name, so as to be reborn there at the end of life. Buddhas of the six directions speak together in praise, to show that this teaching can be trusted.
main.translation:
Thus I have heard. At one time the Buddha was in the country of Shravasti, in the Jeta Grove, in the park of Anathapindika, together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty monks, all great arhats, well known to everyone. There were the elders Shariputra, Maha-Maudgalyayana, Mahakashyapa, Mahakatyayana, Mahakausthila, Revata, Suddhipanthaka, Nanda, Ananda, Rahula, Gavampati, Pindola-Bharadvaja, Kalodayin, Mahakapphina, Vakkula and Aniruddha - such great disciples as these. With them were the bodhisattvas and great beings: Manjushri, prince of the Dharma, the bodhisattva Ajita, the bodhisattva Gandhahastin, and the bodhisattva Nityodyukta, and many other great bodhisattvas like these; and Shakra, lord of the devas, with countless multitudes of devas.

At that time the Buddha spoke to the elder Shariputra: "From here, going west past a hundred thousand million buddha-lands, there is a world called Ultimate Bliss. In that land there is a Buddha named Amitabha, who is teaching the Dharma there now. Shariputra, why is that land called Ultimate Bliss? The living beings of that country have no sufferings at all, and receive only joys; therefore it is called Ultimate Bliss. Again, Shariputra, in the land of Ultimate Bliss there are seven tiers of railings, seven tiers of netting and seven tiers of rows of trees, all encircled by four kinds of jewels; therefore that country is called Ultimate Bliss.

"Again, Shariputra, in the land of Ultimate Bliss there are ponds of the seven jewels, filled with water of the eight virtues, and the floor of every pond is spread with pure golden sand. The steps on the four sides are made of gold, silver, lapis lazuli and crystal joined together; above them are pavilions, adorned with gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, giant clam shell, red pearl and agate. The lotus flowers in the ponds are as large as cartwheels: the blue ones with blue light, the yellow with yellow light, the red with red light, the white with white light, subtle and wondrous, fragrant and pure. Shariputra, the land of Ultimate Bliss has been perfected with such adornments of virtue.

"Again, Shariputra, in that Buddha's land heavenly music is always played, the ground is yellow gold, and six times in the day and night mandarava flowers fall like rain from the sky. The living beings of that land, each morning at dawn, carry in the folds of their robes many wondrous flowers, and make offerings to a hundred thousand million buddhas of other regions; by mealtime they have returned to their own country, and they eat and walk in meditation. Shariputra, the land of Ultimate Bliss has been perfected with such adornments of virtue.

"Furthermore, Shariputra, in that country there are always birds of many strange and wonderful colours: white cranes, peacocks, parrots, sharikas, kalavinkas and two-headed jivajivaka birds. These many birds, six times in the day and night, let out harmonious and graceful sounds, and their sounds proclaim the teachings of the five roots, the five powers, the seven limbs of awakening, the noble eightfold path, and the like. When the living beings of that land hear these sounds, they all call to mind the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha. Shariputra, do not suppose that these birds were truly born as a result of wrongdoing. Why? In that Buddha's land there are no three evil paths. Shariputra, in that Buddha's land even the name of the three evil paths is unknown; how could they exist? All these birds are manifestations made by Amitabha Buddha, who wishes the sound of the Dharma to spread and flow. Shariputra, when a gentle breeze stirs in that Buddha's land, the rows of jewelled trees and the jewelled nets give out subtle and wondrous sounds, as if a hundred thousand kinds of music were played at once; all who hear these sounds spontaneously give rise to the thought of the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha. Shariputra, that Buddha's land has been perfected with such adornments of virtue.

"Shariputra, what do you think? Why is that Buddha called Amitabha? Shariputra, that Buddha's light is limitless, and shines through the lands of the ten directions without obstruction; therefore he is called Amitabha. Again, Shariputra, the life of that Buddha and of his people is limitless and boundless, for innumerable kalpas; therefore he is called Amitabha. Shariputra, it is ten kalpas since Amitabha Buddha became a buddha. Again, Shariputra, that Buddha has limitless, boundless disciples who heard his voice, all of them arhats, more than can be known by counting; and the host of bodhisattvas is just the same. Shariputra, that Buddha's land has been perfected with such adornments of virtue.

"Again, Shariputra, the living beings who are born in the land of Ultimate Bliss are all avaivartikas, never falling back. Among them are many who are one life away from buddhahood; their number is very great, more than can be known by counting, and can be spoken of only as limitless, boundless, innumerable. Shariputra, living beings who hear this should make a vow, wishing to be born in that country. Why? Because they will be able to meet together in one place with such excellent people.

"Shariputra, one cannot be born in that country with few roots of goodness, little merit, and few favourable conditions. Shariputra, if a good man or good woman hears of Amitabha Buddha and holds his name, for one day, two days, three days, four days, five days, six days or seven days, with one mind undisturbed, then when that person comes to the end of life, Amitabha Buddha and the holy assembly will appear before him. When that person dies, his mind is not confused, and he is born at once in Amitabha Buddha's land of Ultimate Bliss. Shariputra, because I see this benefit, I speak these words. If any living being hears this teaching, he should make a vow to be born in that land.

"Shariputra, just as I now praise the benefit of Amitabha Buddha's inconceivable virtues, so in the east there are also Akshobhya Buddha, Sumeru-Sign Buddha, Great Sumeru Buddha, Sumeru-Light Buddha and Wondrous-Sound Buddha, and buddhas like these, as many as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own country puts forth the sign of a long and broad tongue, covering the whole world of three thousand great thousands, and speaks words of truth: 'You living beings, you should believe this sutra, which praises inconceivable virtues and is held in mind and protected by all the buddhas.'

"Shariputra, in the southern world there are Sun-and-Moon-Lamp Buddha, Famed-Light Buddha, Great-Blazing-Shoulders Buddha, Sumeru-Lamp Buddha and Boundless-Diligence Buddha, and buddhas like these, as many as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own country puts forth the sign of a long and broad tongue, covering the whole world of three thousand great thousands, and speaks words of truth: 'You living beings, you should believe this sutra, which praises inconceivable virtues and is held in mind and protected by all the buddhas.'

"Shariputra, in the western world there are Boundless-Life Buddha, Boundless-Form Buddha, Boundless-Banner Buddha, Great-Light Buddha, Great-Radiance Buddha, Jewel-Form Buddha and Pure-Light Buddha, and buddhas like these, as many as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own country puts forth the sign of a long and broad tongue, covering the whole world of three thousand great thousands, and speaks words of truth: 'You living beings, you should believe this sutra, which praises inconceivable virtues and is held in mind and protected by all the buddhas.'

"Shariputra, in the northern world there are Blazing-Shoulders Buddha, Supreme-Sound Buddha, Hard-to-Overcome Buddha, Sun-Born Buddha and Net-Radiance Buddha, and buddhas like these, as many as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own country puts forth the sign of a long and broad tongue, covering the whole world of three thousand great thousands, and speaks words of truth: 'You living beings, you should believe this sutra, which praises inconceivable virtues and is held in mind and protected by all the buddhas.'

"Shariputra, in the world below there are Lion Buddha, Famed Buddha, Famed-Light Buddha, Dharma Buddha, Dharma-Banner Buddha and Dharma-Holder Buddha, and buddhas like these, as many as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own country puts forth the sign of a long and broad tongue, covering the whole world of three thousand great thousands, and speaks words of truth: 'You living beings, you should believe this sutra, which praises inconceivable virtues and is held in mind and protected by all the buddhas.'

"Shariputra, in the world above there are Brahma-Sound Buddha, Constellation-King Buddha, Supreme-Fragrance Buddha, Fragrant-Light Buddha, Great-Blazing-Shoulders Buddha, Many-Coloured-Jewel-Flower-Adorned-Body Buddha, Sala-Tree-King Buddha, Jewel-Flower-Virtue Buddha, Seeing-All-Meanings Buddha and Mount-Sumeru-Like Buddha, and buddhas like these, as many as the sands of the Ganges. Each in his own country puts forth the sign of a long and broad tongue, covering the whole world of three thousand great thousands, and speaks words of truth: 'You living beings, you should believe this sutra, which praises inconceivable virtues and is held in mind and protected by all the buddhas.'

"Shariputra, what do you think? Why is it called the sutra 'held in mind and protected by all the buddhas'? Shariputra, if there are good men and good women who hear this sutra and keep it, and who hear the names of these buddhas, then all those good men and good women are held in mind and protected by all the buddhas, and all of them reach the stage of never falling back from unsurpassed complete awakening. Therefore, Shariputra, all of you should believe and accept my words and what the buddhas say.

"Shariputra, if there are people who have already made the vow, who now make the vow, or who will make the vow, wishing to be born in the land of Amitabha Buddha, then all of them reach the stage of never falling back from unsurpassed complete awakening, and whether they have been born in that land, are being born, or will be born, it is so. Therefore, Shariputra, good men and good women, if they have faith, should make the vow to be born in that land.

"Shariputra, just as I now praise the inconceivable virtues of the buddhas, so those buddhas also praise my inconceivable virtues, and say: 'Shakyamuni Buddha is able to do something extremely difficult and rare. In the Saha land, in the evil age of the five turbidities - the turbidity of the age, of views, of afflictions, of living beings, and of life - he has attained unsurpassed complete awakening, and for the sake of living beings he teaches this Dharma that all the world finds hard to believe.' Shariputra, you should know that I, in the evil age of the five turbidities, have done this difficult thing: I have attained unsurpassed complete awakening, and for the sake of all the world I teach this Dharma that is hard to believe. This is extremely difficult!"

When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, Shariputra and all the monks, and the devas, humans, asuras and others of all the worlds, hearing what the Buddha had said, rejoiced, believed and accepted it, bowed, and departed.

keyLines.line: 從是西方過十萬億佛土，有世界名曰極樂
keyLines.en: From here, going west past a hundred thousand million buddha-lands, there is a world called Ultimate Bliss.
keyLines.note: The opening of the sutra's theme. It places Ultimate Bliss in the west, a hundred thousand million buddha-lands from our Saha world, and as a land where a buddha is teaching 'at this very moment'.

keyLines.line: 其國眾生無有眾苦，但受諸樂，故名極樂
keyLines.en: The living beings of that country have no sufferings at all, and receive only joys; therefore it is called Ultimate Bliss.
keyLines.note: This explains the name 'Ultimate Bliss': no suffering at all, only joy. The sutra then describes the splendour of the land in detail with its ponds of seven treasures, water of the eight virtues and great lotuses.

keyLines.line: 彼佛光明無量，照十方國無所障礙，是故號為阿彌陀
keyLines.en: That Buddha's light is limitless, and shines through the lands of the ten directions without obstruction; therefore he is called Amitabha.
keyLines.note: This explains the name 'Amitabha': limitless light and limitless life. The sutra gives light and life as the two reasons for the Buddha's name.

keyLines.line: 不可以少善根福德因緣得生彼國
keyLines.en: One cannot be born in that country with few roots of goodness, little merit, and few favourable conditions.
keyLines.note: Rebirth in Ultimate Bliss takes enough roots of goodness, merit and conditions, and cannot be taken lightly. The very next lines give the method: 'hold the name'.

keyLines.line: 聞說阿彌陀佛，執持名號，若一日、若二日、若三日、若四日、若五日、若六日、若七日，一心不亂
keyLines.en: Hears of Amitabha Buddha and holds his name, for one day, two days ... or seven days, with one mind undisturbed.
keyLines.note: The central practice of the sutra: to call the name of Amitabha with a single mind for one to seven days until the mind is 'one and undisturbed'. At death the Buddha and the holy assembly appear to welcome the person. This passage is the main scriptural basis for the Pure Land practice of holding the name.

keyLines.line: 阿彌陀佛與諸聖眾，現在其前
keyLines.en: Amitabha Buddha and the holy assembly will appear before him.
keyLines.note: The signs at the moment of death: Amitabha and the holy assembly appear and welcome the person, so that the mind is not confused and rebirth goes smoothly.

keyLines.line: 汝等眾生，當信是稱讚不可思議功德一切諸佛所護念經
keyLines.en: You living beings, you should believe this sutra, which praises inconceivable virtues and is held in mind and protected by all the buddhas.
keyLines.note: Buddhas of the east, south, west, north, below and above each put forth a broad and long tongue and urge belief in unison. The sutra is protected by all the buddhas, and so is also called by the title of Xuanzang's version, 'Sutra on the Buddhas' Praise and Acceptance of the Pure Land'.

keyLines.line: 釋迦牟尼佛能為甚難希有之事
keyLines.en: Shakyamuni Buddha is able to do something extremely difficult and rare.
keyLines.note: In turn the buddhas praise Shakyamuni for teaching, in the evil age of the five turbidities, this Dharma that the whole world finds hard to believe. It shows how rare and excellent this path is.

glossary.note: A translation of the Sanskrit Sukhavati, 'having bliss'. It is the Pure Land of Amitabha, where there is no suffering and only joy.
From the Sanskrit Amitabha ('limitless light') and Amitayus ('limitless life'). He is the teacher of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The great disciple of the Buddha who was foremost in wisdom. In this sutra the Buddha speaks to him without being asked, so it is called the sutra 'spoken unasked'.
To 'hold' is to keep steady with a single mind, and not to let it slip. It means calling the name of Amitabha with undivided attention: the practice of holding the name (chi ming nian fo).

glossary.en: yixin bu luan - one mind undisturbed
glossary.note: A state of calling the Buddha's name with unified, undisturbed attention. Commentators have long distinguished the 'one mind of practice' (thought following thought without a break) from the 'one mind of principle' (realising the true nature of things).
Transcription of the Sanskrit avaivartika, 'non-regression': the stage at which practice no longer slips back and Buddhahood is certain.

glossary.en: yisheng buchu - one life from buddhahood
glossary.note: A bodhisattva who is one life away from taking the place of a buddha, such as Maitreya. The sutra means that in Ultimate Bliss there are many great bodhisattvas close to becoming buddhas.

glossary.en: wuzhuo e shi - the evil age of the five turbidities
glossary.note: The five kinds of defilement of the Saha world: the turbidity of the age (kalpa), of views, of afflictions, of living beings and of life.

main.background: This is one of the 'Three Pure Land Sutras', the main scriptural basis of the Pure Land school (the others are the Longer Sutra of Limitless Life and the Sutra of Contemplation on Limitless Life). It was translated by Kumarajiva in the Later Qin dynasty (384-417) in the fourth year of the Hongshi era (402), and is also called the Shorter Sutra of Limitless Life. It is short and is often used in morning and evening recitation. It is also unusual in that nobody asks the Buddha a question: it is a sutra which the Buddha speaks unasked, describing the Pure Land throughout in words.
